blocks.heading: LESSON 2 · WHY CLOUD WON
blocks.board_text:
Today:
• Speed to market
• Cost shape (pay for use)
• Survive traffic spikes

Finova-shaped stakes with ₹.
blocks.ren_voice: Lesson 2. Companies do not buy cloud for fashion. They buy speed, flexible cost, and survival when traffic explodes.

blocks.heading: BEFORE vs AFTER
blocks.board_text:
Before cloud:
• Crores upfront for hardware
• Weeks to procure
• Guess capacity wrong → crash or waste

With cloud:
• Start near zero
• Scale in minutes
• Pay for what you use
blocks.ren_voice: Before cloud, a startup spent months and crores before writing product code. Guess ten servers — too few and you crash on launch day; too many and you bleed money idle. Cloud lets you start small and expand in minutes.

check_question.question: Name two business reasons companies moved to cloud.
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Speed and flexible cost — or survival under spikes. Good.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Think time-to-launch and what happens when traffic goes 20x overnight.

blocks.heading: COST SHAPE
blocks.board_text:
CapEx: big buy now, hope you guessed right.
OpEx: monthly bill that follows usage.

Cloud shifts most infrastructure spend toward OpEx.
blocks.ren_voice: CapEx is buying a generator. OpEx is the electricity bill. Cloud mostly feels like OpEx — the bill follows demand. That is why CFOs care.

blocks.heading: FINOVA LENS
blocks.board_text:
Finova launches a festival payment promo.
Traffic can 15x for six hours.
Physical rack: crash or overbuy.
Cloud: scale up for the window, scale down after.
blocks.ren_voice: Finova runs festival traffic. Six hours of madness. With cloud they add capacity for the window and release it after. That flexibility is why they pay AWS.

blocks.ren_voice: Companies pay for speed and survival. Next lesson — how the technology delivers that.
